label: Create a text file with any name you like that ends in '.FDR'.
This is a flight data recorder file, storing data from an actual Flight Data Recorder, or perhaps just a simulated flight.
See the INSTRUCTIONS folder for a sample FDR file. Here are the allowable FDR entries:
COMM: any comment
ACFT: the aircraft file to use, with directory path from X-Plane itself, for example: Aircraft/Heavy Metal/Boeing 747.acf
TAIL: the tail number of the aircraft, for example: N8141Q. This line must come AFTER the ACFT line.
TIME: the ZULU time of the beginning of the flight, for example: 18:54:32
DATE: the date of the flight, for example: 03/05/02
PRES: the sea-level pressure during the flight in inches HG, for example: 29.92
TEMP: the sea-level temperature during the flight in degrees F, for example: 65
WIND: the wind during the flight in degrees then knots, for example: 230,17
CALI: the ACTUAL takeoff or touchdown longitude, latitude, and elevation in feet for calibration, for example: -118.34, 34.57, 456. This calibrates to X-Plane scenery.
WARN: warning WAV file, with directory path from X-Plane itself, at a given time, for example: 10,aural_alarm.wav
TEXT: spoken text to be read aloud by the computer at a given time, for example: 10,Copilot left the cockpit here.
MARK: text marker to appear in the time slider at a given time, for example: 10,Approach began here.
EVNT: flight path to be hilighted at a given time for the event duration, for example: 10,5
DATA: a bunch of comma-delimited floating-point numbers, following the labels in the screen below.
Once you have clicked below to read in the file, close this window and play the flight in X-Plane with the VCR buttons at the top of the screen.
